# YM40: 洞天深处 Dongtian Shenchu, "The Depth of the Vault of Heaven"

Malone calls it The Palace School, the Princes' Residences, and Studios.

Wave 2 · Yuanming Yuan · 3D: `/reconstruction/3d.html?b=YM40` · Page: `/scenes/#YM40` · Row: `research/buildings/YM40-dongtian-shenchu/`

## What it was

洞天深处 Dongtian Shenchu, west and a little south of 如意馆, in the south-east of the garden: in front the 四所, four courts of the princes' lodgings on two east-west lanes and one north-south lane, with 福园门 Fuyuan Men before them; west of them the princes' school with 前垂天贶, 中天景物 and 后天不老 on an axis and 斯文在兹 on the east, which held a shrine of Confucius (S05 j82:28b-29a; E2089, S361). 如意馆 was the court painters' workshop where Castiglione and Attiret worked (E2089). Malone puts 福园门 in the outer wall about 300 yards east of 大宫门 (E0385, E2088, S02). Burned October 1860 (S02 pp.187-188).

From the inventory row: **changed** Four courts rebuilt as two groups (S41); 如意馆 new layout pasted on plan (S02 p.96 n.); 1846: east and west four courts reduced to two; **destroyed** 1860 (S05, S02, S08, S41, S01, S337).

## The scene itself

### The leaf of 1744, its poem and preface

Preface of 1744: "縁溪而東徑曲折如蟻盤短椽陿室於奥為宜" (S05 j82:29b): along the stream eastward the path winds like an ant's spiral; small rooms with short rafters suit the deep corner; a little south is 前垂天贶, 'my brothers' and my old reading room', named by Yongzheng. He ends: 'may I be a gentleman-scholar, not a wanderer'.

### How later sources differ

S01 labels 乐道堂 (YM40-N01) and 东所 (YM40-N02), not in S05: later residents' names. 63 rows in the inventory, the most of any scene here, mostly unnamed courtyard ranges of the 四所. The gate is written 福元门 on S01 and 福园门 in the texts; a Yangshi Lei plan (sheet 043-002) names the place 福元四所, so the plan form is itself Qing (E0382, S337). Malone says the woodcut of scene 40 shows the gate and the painting does not (E0385, S02). S360 has only a short undated note (E2092).
